title: Polynomial mixing at the four-state Potts critical point
formal: Do there exist absolute constants C,c>0 such that t_mix(1/4)≤C L^c for critical four-state Swendsen–Wang dynamics on every square torus of side L≥3?
definitions: For integer L≥3, the square torus has vertices (Z/LZ)^2 and an undirected edge between vertices differing by 1 or −1 in exactly one coordinate and agreeing in the other; duplicate edges are suppressed. A q-state spin configuration assigns a color in {1,…,q} to each vertex. At inverse temperature β, μ(σ)=Z^(−1)exp(β∑_{uv∈E}1[σ(u)=σ(v)]), with no external field. A Swendsen–Wang step independently retains each monochromatic edge with probability p=1−exp(−β), retains no other edges, and independently assigns each resulting connected component a uniform color in {1,…,q}. Singletons are components as well. The critical inverse temperature in this normalization is β_c(q)=log(1+sqrt(q)). Here q=4, β=log 3 and p=2/3. For a finite-state transition matrix P with target distribution μ, define t_mix(1/4)=min{t∈N: max_x (1/2)∑_y |P^t(x,y)−μ(y)|≤1/4}, with value infinity if no such t exists. One step means the entire stated update, not one vertex recoloring.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated proposition or its negation for the specified model. The polynomial exponent and constant must not depend on L. A quasipolynomial bound L^{O(log L)} does not suffice.
context: The critical torus results distinguish q=4 from the polynomial regime already treated for smaller q. The comparison between local and cluster chains supplies background, not an exponent determination.
why: This isolates the unresolved critical sampling threshold between established polynomial and quasipolynomial guarantees.

import_provenance.original_statement: Does Swendsen–Wang dynamics for the zero-field ferromagnetic four-state Potts model on an L×L square torus at its critical temperature mix in L^O(1) full cluster updates? This is the remaining four-state case of the predicted polynomial critical slowdown, beyond the known quasipolynomial bound.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: This is an editorial continuation of Chayes’s work on critical Potts dynamics; polynomial bounds for two and three states do not settle four states.

sentences: Four colors interact ferromagnetically on a periodic square grid.
A step opens same-color edges and recolors all resulting clusters.
The inverse temperature is log 3 in the specified Potts normalization.
Mixing is measured from the worst starting spin configuration.
The question asks for a fixed polynomial in the side length.
